checks: No eclipse at 2 of 15 covered epochs where the 8.00059 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: The automated TESS photometry pipeline has identified TIC 376932771 as a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 8.000586 days. The system shows a primary eclipse with 3.69% dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 6.9 sigma significance. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 27.2, though the centroid offset of 2.4 arcseconds warrants attention. One data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, which the analysis attributes to the system's true period being double the initial detection value. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the detection achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of 598 in the box-least-squares search, suggesting a robust photometric signal worthy of further investigation.
